detectors.rationale: Binding v-html to a user-controlled prop (userBio) sets innerHTML directly with no sanitization, allowing stored/reflected XSS if the value contains markup or script; the safe idiom uses Vue's default text interpolation ({{ userBio }}), which HTML-escapes the value and never sets innerHTML, so no markup is ever injected.

Binding :href directly to a raw user-controlled value (userProvidedUrl) with no scheme check lets an attacker supply a javascript: URL that executes on click; the safe idiom routes the value through a safeHref() allowlist function inside the template expression, which the regex (requiring a bare identifier with no call syntax) correctly does not match.

Binding :src directly to a raw user-controlled value (userProvidedImageUrl) with no scheme validation allows a javascript:/data: URI or arbitrary external resource load; the safe idiom wraps the value in a safeSrc() allowlist function call in the template, which the bare-identifier regex correctly does not match.

Declaring reactive({...}) at module scope (unindented top-level const) in an SSR entry point creates one object shared by every concurrent request handled by the long-lived Node.js process, causing cross-request state pollution (one user's data leaking to another); the safe idiom moves the identical reactive() call inside the per-request render() function, so each request gets its own isolated instance and the regex's module-scope (column-0, unindented) anchor no longer matches.
